title: install-runtime-failure-patterns-vpc-checks
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a working playbook for common install/runtime failures observed in Private deployments (VPC and on-prem packages). It focuses on triage heuristics, Terraform module quirks, preflight / post-upgrade smoke tests, and repeatable remediation steps. Intended users: SREs on-call, solutions engineers running customer upgrades, and platform engineers debugging nodes and the serving runtime.

Quick triage flow (one-page):
1) Gather context: deployment type (VPC vs on-prem), upgrade vs fresh install, agent logs, terraform apply output, kube events, host tooling (docker/containerd, nvidia-smi).
2) Confirm control-plane reachability: can we terraform state list / kubectl get pods? If both failing, suspect network/TF state issues.
3) If pods create then crash -> inspect pod logs, describe, node status, and node-level drivers (GPU) or cgroups.
4) If terraform fails during apply -> capture plan diff, provider version, and state-lock status.
5) Use smoke-test checklist (below) to quickly verify core pieces.

Common failure patterns and first-actions:
- Terraform apply fails with "Error: state lock" or "unable to acquire state lock":
  First action: terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID> against the same backend. Confirm no concurrent CI/CD run is active. Check S3/Consul/PG backend health.
  Log snippets to capture: full terraform error, backend diagnostics, last successful apply timestamp.

- Provider/plugin mismatch (eg: aws provider v4 vs v5) or provider not found:
  First action: inspect .terraform.lock.hcl and terraform version (terraform --version). Re-run terraform init -upgrade to refresh providers. If module pins a provider, consider applying in a separate workspace with matched terraform.

- Resource quota / IAM denies during apply (403):
  First action: run aws sts get-caller-identity (or cloud provider equivalent) from tooling runner, test specific API call (eg iam:CreateRole). Check assume-role configurations and KMS access for S3 state.

- K8s ImagePullBackOff / ErrImagePull after upgrade:
  First action: kubectl describe pod <pod> to see image pull errors. Common root causes: private registry auth, image tag mismatch (e.g., manifest digest changed), or air-gapped nodes missing registry mirror.
  Fix: ensure imagePullSecrets present, verify registry mirror DNS/network path, or re-tag and push image to allowed registry.

- CrashLoopBackOff in inference-runtime container:
  First action: kubectl logs -c inference-runtime <pod> --previous (if restarting) and check JVM/py stack traces or the runtime's STDOUT. Look for OOM, invalid model manifests, plugin load failures, or KV cache corruption.
  Node-level checks: dmesg for OOM killer, free -m, nvidia-smi (if GPU).

- Liveness probe flapping after upgrade:
  First action: inspect readiness/liveness endpoints (curl -sS http://<pod-ip>:<probe-port>/live). If probe is returning 503 due to long model load times, increase probe timeout or pre-warm models during rollout.

- Model artifacts mismatch or checksum error at startup:
  First action: check object store (S3/GCS/MinIO) paths and object checksums. If using content-addressable storage, verify digest in model manifest matches stored object. Re-sync artifacts if mismatch.

- GPU driver / CUDA mismatch:
  First action: run nvidia-smi and check driver version vs expected. For container runtimes, run nvidia-container-cli --load-kmods and compare container base image CUDA toolkit version. If mismatched, either update host drivers or use a compatible runtime image (alternate tag).

Terraform module notes (gotchas we see frequently):
- Module variable collisions: several older TF modules used global variable names like region or cluster_name. When composing modules, avoid setting vars at root unless namespaced (use module.<name>.var).
- State drift with onprem: local resources (baremetal inventory) often drift. Keep a short design doc in Git (module usage examples) and record manual changes in a 'manual_changes' tag in state notes.
- Force unlock procedures: always verify no CI token active. Steps:
  1) terraform plan -refresh=false -lock=false to see pending changes.
  2) terraform force-unlock <ID>.
  3) Re-run terraform apply with -auto-approve only after confirming plan.
- Provider upgrades: pin provider major versions in top-level registry modules and test in a dedicated dev workspace before applying to prod.

Upgrade plan and rollback (short):
- Preflight (immutable snapshot): capture current terraform state snapshot and kube resource exports. Example commands:
  - terraform state pull > state-YYYYMMDD.json
  - kubectl get all --all-namespaces -o yaml > all-resources-YYYYMMDD.yaml
- Canary: apply to a small subset (canary nodes or dedicated namespace). Redirect 5-10% of traffic. Run full smoke tests.
- Gradual rollout: 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 10-15 minute observation windows depending on model load times.
- Rollback: two options depending on failure type:
  - Config rollback: terraform apply using last-known-good variables or module tag (example: terraform apply -var 'image_tag=2025-09-11-rc3').
  - Manifest rollback: kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name> --namespace=<ns> or helm rollback <release> <revision>.
  Always run post-rollback smoke tests to verify.

Smoke-test checklist (fast verifications to run after install/upgrade):
1) Control plane health:
   - terraform state list (should return expected resources)
   - kubectl get nodes (all nodes Ready)
   - kubectl get pods -A (no pods in CrashLoopBackOff/Error)
2) Networking & DNS:
   - curl -I https://internal-service.<cluster>.svc.cluster.local (from busybox pod) -> expect 200/302 as appropriate
   - dig <registry-mirror> from nodes -> IP resolves, TTL sensible
3) Storage & artifacts:
   - aws s3 ls s3://<bucket>/models/<model-id>/manifest.json
   - md5sum/sha256sum check of a known artifact
4) Serving runtime smoke run:
   - Send small request to hosted endpoint or port-forward to pod: curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"input":"hello"}' http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -> expect 200 and valid JSON with tokens.
   - Validate streaming works with a sample curl streaming test (if enabled).
5) Observability and logs:
   - Ensure metrics exporter scraping is active: curl http://prometheus-scrape-target:9102/metrics -> metrics show tokens_served counter incrementing when tests run.
   - Check that logs for runtime are being forwarded to customer log sink (grep for test request id).
6) GPU / runtime specialized checks (if applicable):
   - nvidia-smi shows expected GPU memory and processes during test
   - docker ps / crictl ps show runtime container with GPU flag enabled

Example commands (cheat sheet):
- Lock diagnostics: terraform force-unlock -force <LOCK_ID>
- Re-init providers: terraform init -reconfigure -upgrade
- View pod events: kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <ns>
- Previous logs: kubectl logs <pod> -c inference-runtime --previous -n <ns>
- Get node dmesg: ssh node-01 'sudo dmesg | tail -n 200'
- Check driver: ssh node-01 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,gpu_name --format=csv'
- Check object store: aws s3api head-object --bucket <bucket> --key models/<id>/weights.pt

Escalation matrix and judgement calls:
- If terraform backend shows corruption or backend errors (S3 5xx, DB connection failures), stop any further applies and notify infra ops; consider restoring state from snapshot and opening storage provider support ticket.
- If widespread node-level OOMs or kernel panic observed, escalate to SRE Lead and schedule maintenance window.
- If a model artifact mismatch affects multiple tenants, treat as high-severity and follow customer incident SLA.

Notes from prior incidents (brief):
- Incident: model load OOM after switch to quantized runtime image; root cause was missing LD_PRELOAD for jemalloc. Remediation: roll image back, patch helm chart to include env var LD_PRELOAD, run canary.
- Incident: terraform plan succeeded but apply hung due to IAM rate-limit; fix included rate-limiting retries in operator and breaking resource creation into smaller batches.

Appendix: quick heuristics mapping error strings -> immediate next command
- "context deadline exceeded" -> curl internal endpoints from node to test network (curl -sv)
- "no matching manifest for linux/amd64 in the manifest list entries" -> check image tag and multi-arch support, revert to amd64-only image or rebuild
- "permission denied" on model artifact download -> test S3 credentials and KMS decrypt using aws kms decrypt call; check bucket policy

How to contribute to this doc:
- Add short, repeatable commands and exact log snippets you've seen. Keep entries concise. Mark any verified fixes with the date and your initials.

End of doc.
